How it works

Three steps from install to session.

KarCast does not add a dongle. It uses the phone you already have and the browser already in the car.

  1. 01

    Install KarCast on Android

    Download the app, finish setup, and keep Android Auto ready on the phone.

  2. 02

    Join the same Wi-Fi path

    Share the phone hotspot or connect the car and phone to the same local network.

  3. 03

    Open the address in the car

    Type the address KarCast shows, start the session, and keep your attention on the road.

Traffic for the session stays on the local Wi-Fi path. You do not need a mobile-data tunnel to keep maps and media on the dash.

FAQ

Straight answers before you install.

What is KarCast?

KarCast brings the Android Auto experience from your Android phone to a compatible car browser. You follow a short setup, connect over Wi-Fi, and open the address shown in the app.

Does it work while driving?

Once the session is running it can stay on the dash. Set it up while parked. Keep your attention on the road and follow local law. KarCast is not a license to browse or watch video in motion.

Which phones and cars are compatible?

You need an Android phone with Android Auto, a Wi-Fi path, and a car browser that can open a local address. Tesla’s browser is a common target. Fit still varies by car software — use the checker above or write to support.

Do I need a hotspot or internet?

You need a local network path between the phone and the car browser. A phone hotspot is the usual way. The session itself is local. Apps on the phone may still need their own data for live traffic or streaming.

Does it support iPhone or CarPlay?

No. KarCast is built around Android Auto on an Android phone. It is an independent product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google, Apple, or Tesla.

How does audio work?

Media and guidance stay tied to the Android Auto session on the phone. How sound reaches the car speakers depends on your car and Bluetooth or built-in audio path.
